What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 66-year-old woman of Turkish descent
Admission: January 2015
Discharge: September 2015

Hospital Course: 

Admitted for follow-up after kidney transplantation, the patient presented with a rise in creatinine and urinary protein-creatinine ratio, and later developed microhaematuria. Biopsy showed extracapillary proliferative changes, and positive autoimmune serology for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, indicative of AAV granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Treatment included intravenous prednisolone, rituximab, plasma exchange and maintenance therapy. However, corticosteroid-related diabetes mellitus, pneumonia, CMV reactivation, and donor-specific HLA antibodies emerged. Despite interventions, including resection of the transplanted kidney, regular hemodialysis became necessary. The patient experienced no further clinically significant vasculitis activity during two years of follow-up. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Significant Hospital Course Events: 

- Elevated creatinine and urinary protein-creatinine ratio, microhaematuria
- Biopsy showed extracapillary proliferative changes consistent with pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis and AAV
- Positive autoimmune serology for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
- Treatment with intravenous prednisolone, rituximab, plasma exchange and maintenance therapy
- Complications included corticosteroid-related diabetes mellitus, pneumonia, CMV reactivation, and donor-specific HLA antibodies.
- Regular hemodialysis was commenced four months after the initial presentation.
- Transplanted kidney was resected due to new development of donor-specific HLA antibodies and persistent haematuria.
- PR3-ANCA remained positive, but declined steadily.
- No further clinical vasculitis activity during follow-up for two years.

text:
# ICD-10-AM Principal Diagnosis: M31.3 Wegener granulomatosis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis)

## Why this code

- **Condition chiefly responsible for the admission:** ANCA-associated vasculitis (PR3-ANCA positive) causing pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in the transplanted kidney. This is what triggered the work-up and the main treatment (IV prednisolone, rituximab, plasma exchange).
- **Kidney involvement:** M31.3 is the dagger code. It is paired with the asterisk code **N08.5\*** (glomerular disorders in systemic connective tissue disorders). Under dagger/asterisk convention, the dagger (aetiology) code is sequenced first.
- **Vasculitis, not rejection:** The core problem is the vasculitis (new or recurrent) in the graft. Under ACS guidance, a disease occurring in a transplanted organ is coded to the disease itself rather than to T86.1 (kidney transplant failure/rejection) as principal. Sites can apply this differently, so it is worth checking the relevant ACS and any local guidance.

## Suggested additional codes (depending on documentation and local rules)

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| N08.5\* | Glomerular disorder in systemic connective tissue disorder |
| T86.1 | Kidney transplant failure (donor-specific HLA antibodies, graft resection) |
| Z94.0 | Kidney transplant status |
| E09.x | Drug-induced diabetes mellitus, plus Y42.0 (glucocorticoids, adverse effect in therapeutic use) |
| J18.9 (or more specific) | Pneumonia |
| B25.x / B27.1 | CMV disease/reactivation, as documented |
| N18.5 + Z49.1 / Z99.2 | End-stage kidney disease and dialysis |

Procedure codes would also be needed for the transplant nephrectomy, plasmapheresis, haemodialysis and the biopsy.
